_comment: Programme-level review of Securitize Stocks CETs, separate from issuer-sponsored SECZ. Exact mint identity is verified; account-specific and jurisdiction-specific order terms are not.
issuer: Securitize Stocks — Convertible Entitlement Tokens administered by Securitize Markets, LLC
statusNote: Official catalogue lists 12 new stock mints; finalized AAPL/USDC swap observed. Individual eligibility and DRS execution not tested.
products: CET launch: AAPL, AMZN, CRCL, META, MSFT, MSTR, NFLX, NVDA, PLTR, SPCX and TSLA; launch names GOOG but the live catalogue instead lists GOOGL.
SECZ is an issuer-sponsored share covered separately under securitize. ETs have different ownership and cash-exit terms and are outside this CET review.
issuingEntity: Securitize Markets, LLC is the contractual securities intermediary and broker. Apple and the other referenced companies issue the underlying shares; the launch does not make them sponsors of these tokens.
entityJurisdiction: United States broker; Securitize Europe Brokerage and Markets, S.V., S.A. separately provides EU investment services. Exact account contracting chain must be checked for each jurisdiction.
governingLaw: Customer Brokerage Account Agreement: New York law, Article 8 securities entitlements and FINRA or eligible exchange arbitration. EU platform terms use Spanish law; they do not establish that every EU customer has the same direct SM account claim.
regulatoryStatus: SM identifies itself as an SEC-registered broker-dealer and FINRA/SIPC member. Registration is not an approval of each product or a guarantee that a wallet-held position qualifies for SIPC. Access requires eligibility checks.
holderClaim: The CET disclosure identifies the customer as beneficial owner of a share position credited on SM books, separate from proprietary holdings. The brokerage agreement makes those books authoritative: an on-chain transfer is an instruction, and the legal entitlement moves when SM records the corresponding debit and credit. A CET is distinct from an issuer-sponsored registered share and from the separately defined ET.
underlyingCustodian: SM holds the underlying book-entry share position for the customer and may use nominees or third-party custodians. No exact stock-by-stock custody account, subcustodian agreement or independent reconciliation was located. Do not attribute the new CET pool to RQD from another programme.

collateral.composition: Underlying listed shares associated with CET positions; actual reconciliation not independently verified.
collateral.rehypothecation: Launch states no lending; disclosure restricts underlying transfers while CETs exist and excludes use for unrelated proprietary trading. The brokerage agreement still grants SM a lien for customer obligations; this is not proof of an unencumbered upstream custody chain.

custodyVerification.frequency: No public independent reserve-report cadence located
custodyVerification.notes: Public mint supply and the issuer catalogue verify deployed token identity, not matching shares in custody. No independent dated CET reserve statement located.

securityInterest.holder: No separately granted holder collateral security package reviewed; Article 8 property rights are a different legal mechanism.
securityInterest.priority: Article 8 section 8-503 normally separates financial assets from intermediary creditors, subject to section 8-511. SM also has a customer-obligation lien under the brokerage agreement; upstream liens unverified.

redemption.eligibility: Approved, KYC/AML-cleared customer. Conventional share transfer requires a DTCC-member receiving broker willing to accept the position; SM procedures and compliance restrictions apply.
redemption.rails: CETs have no contractual cash redemption. Exit by selling on the platform, or request book-entry conversion and DRS transfer to an accepting broker independently of issuer tokenization. Conversion into an issuer-sponsored token separately requires the underlying issuer to adopt a programme and authorize SM. DRS execution has not been independently observed.
redemption.fees: CET/ET trading commission 0.1% of gross value. DRS transfer-out $30 plus receiving-broker charges. Wallet gas, stablecoin conversion and corporate-action charges can also apply.
redemption.minimum: Disclosure says typically 1 USDC but product-specific; current order screen controls. Catalogue settlement asset shows minLimit 10. No authenticated order minimum verified.

transferRestrictions.mechanism: default-frozen token accounts, linked approved wallets and broker compliance controls

corporateActions: SM processes mandatory actions against underlying shares and updates accounts/tokens; voluntary actions require timely elections. Cash distributions use the settlement stablecoin, net of charges and tax. A processing fee can consume a small dividend. Votes are expected to pass through; SM handles uninstructed votes under a policy available on request. Delivery performance and that policy were not verified.

pricing.notes: Public FAQ quotes NBBO with a 10 bps execution-protection band and 04:00–17:30 ET trading hours. AAPL/USDC execution was observed on-chain. Continuous 24/7 liquidity and unrestricted arbitrage are not established.

venues: Securitize Stocks / SM execution venue; AAPL swap observed on Solana. Broader NYSE/OKX/Ripple/Aave integrations in the announcement are plans, not verified live CET routes.

keyGovernance.evidence: All 12 new mints share delegate, pause, metadata and scaled-UI authority Ui3bQKRdTzNRv21sPuXTgmzuz4dLh3sH3B9Y5sxapSR. Finalized read at slot 454614970: funded system-owned zero-data account. This is one on-chain authority address, not proof of one human or absence of off-chain MPC. AAPL mint/freeze authority account is absent; its signing programme and upgrade path were not resolved. The shared administrative authority is on the Ed25519 curve; AAPL mint/freeze authority is off-curve, checked with the existing solana-address module. No claim is made about the number of people or off-chain approvals needed to sign.

findings.statement: Token movement alone is not the final legal transfer: SM must make the book-entry debit and credit. Reconciliation failure can separate the wallet display from the enforceable account position.
CET cash redemption is excluded. The alternative is a platform sale or a documented transfer into conventional shares; a successful DRS exit was not observed.

The documents expect customer-securities treatment for underlying CET positions but exclude held-away self-custody assets from SIPC through SM. The treatment of a wallet-held CET and its retained underlying share needs account-specific clarification.
The 1:1 and no-lending statements are issuer assertions. A live mint and trade do not prove the required share pool exists, is fully reconciled or is free of upstream liens.

All 12 mints share the permanent-delegate/pause/scaled-UI authority Ui3bQKRdTzNRv21sPuXTgmzuz4dLh3sH3B9Y5sxapSR. Accounts start frozen. Token self-custody does not remove these intervention powers; signing policy is unverified.
CET terms provide DRS transfer to an accepting DTCC-member broker even without issuer adoption of tokenization. Published transfer fee is $30, subject to procedures and receiving-broker fees.

discrepancies.title: Launch names GOOG; official catalogue lists GOOGL

reality.text: Catalogue lists GOOGL, Alphabet Class A, ISIN US02079K3059 / CUSIP 02079K305, at mint 2qXFRgxeYUkc19JBAzRvZZReAhVTWFd31m9qM2C3a2GK.

discrepancies.impact: Share classes carry different voting rights. Index the published GOOGL address without inventing a GOOG mint or assuming a GOOG order disclosure covers it.
discrepancies.resolutionCondition: Issuer corrects the launch list or publishes consistent per-mint share-class and order terms.

openQuestions: Which exact custody accounts and subcustodians hold each share pool, and where is an independently dated share-to-token reconciliation?
How are customer securities and SIPC eligibility recorded when the CET is in a self-custody wallet? The agreement distinguishes custody models but does not resolve that combined case.
Which signed product/order disclosure binds each mint and customer, especially GOOGL and EU users? The catalogue does not carry those agreements.
How long does DRS conversion take, which brokers accept fractional positions, and has the exit actually completed for a CET holder?
What signing policy governs the shared administrative key, and which programmes and upgrade keys control minting and thawing?
What does the proxy voting policy require, and what corporate-action processing fees apply?
The disclosure calls CETs Convertible; the brokerage agreement mainly calls them Custodial. Confirm that the executed agreement and order disclosures map those terms to the same product.
What happens if SM books and chain diverge or SM becomes unavailable? No product-specific tested recovery procedure or court decision located.
Which jurisdictions and investor categories are currently eligible for each CET? No comprehensive current admission matrix was verified.

whatIf.outcome: Article 8 provides property protections for financial assets held for entitlement holders, subject to priority rules. Actual pool completeness, customer obligations, custody model and SIPC eligibility determine recovery. No CET-specific insolvency outcome verified.
whatIf.locator: section 8-503; see agreement SIPC and lien provisions

whatIf.outcome: No cash redemption right. A conventional-share DRS route is documented but depends on SM compliance processing and an accepting broker; no alternative autonomous execution route verified.
The disclosure describes SM as the only current secondary venue and imposes no market-making obligation. A DRS conversion request is a different exit route, not guaranteed immediate liquidity.

The permanent delegate can move or burn tokens without the holder signature, subject to token-program checks. Recovery and reconciliation after compromise are unverified; self-custody alone does not prevent intervention.

Public documents promise corresponding share positions, but no independent reconciliation or CET-specific shortfall waterfall was located. Article 8 gives a pro-rata interest in the asset pool; recoverability remains fact-dependent.
